notes: kb/Work PB5163 LANDED: an empty argument list after a function name is refused at --std 85 with COBOL0900 (construct function-empty-argument-list-2002, gated by recognition in VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitFunctionCall at the empty list's left parenthesis), so FUNCTION RANDOM ( ) is refused at 85 and accepted from 2002 (ISO/IEC 1989:2002 8.4.2.2.2 SR4's NOTE writes FUNCTION RANDOM (); Annex F.1 item 20). The printed forms FUNCTION RANDOM and FUNCTION RANDOM (argument-1) still compile. The row's earlier reading: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1989:A.2.35.2 prints "FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( argument-1 ) ]": the parentheses are written only with an argument in them, as the function-identifier format of §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.2 also requires ("[ ( { argument-1 } … ) ]"). Both printed forms conform at 85: the catalog row (Build) gives RANDOM zero or one argument, and BindFunctionResult refuses two with COBOL1504 (the witness); RANDOM without FUNCTION is refused with COBOL1543. The part not implemented is the refusal of empty parentheses: the functionCall rule makes the argument list optional inside the parentheses (the form §2023:15.75.2 adds, "[ ( [ argument-1 ] ) ]") and neither BindIntrinsic nor BindFunctionResult asks the edition, so FUNCTION RANDOM ( ) compiles at --std 85. The same holds for the 1989 functions without arguments: FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE ( ) and FUNCTION WHEN-COMPILED ( ) compile at 85.

next.reason: 1985: "FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( argument-1 ) ]"; 2023: "FUNCTION RANDOM [ ( [ argument-1 ] ) ]". The 2023 format makes argument-1 optional inside the parentheses, so FUNCTION RANDOM ( ) with empty parentheses is now accepted. The 1985 format does not allow that form.
